title: Agent-first analysis roadmap: raw mapping, bounded inspection, diagnostics, and workflow features
description:
# binscout — agent analysis roadmap

Date: 2026-10-15. Repository: `/Users/mimi/work/rsdbg`.
Implementation progress: **0/17 steps complete (0%)**. Planning and backlog creation are not implementation.
Beads: epic **`rsdbg-0vt`**, children **`rsdbg-0vt.1`–`rsdbg-0vt.17`**. Child suffix matches the numbered step below. All implementation issues are open; no work is claimed or implemented. The graph has 31 blocking edges in addition to parent-child links.

Planning complete: current code/backlog reviewed, duplicate checks performed, user decisions recorded, detailed issues created, and dependency ordering recorded. Ready first: **`rsdbg-0vt.1`** (contracts) and **`rsdbg-0vt.2`** (mapping-aware cache identity).

## Current state

`binscout` 0.3.0 is a Rust 2024 library with JSON CLI and 13 stdio MCP tools. It loads ELF/PE/Mach-O/LE/raw binaries, discovers functions and CFGs, extracts strings and xrefs, emits a deliberately minimal IR, and saves analysis plus annotations in a redb sidecar. Synthetic integration tests cover format parsing, budgets, stale snapshots, query bounds, and both interfaces.

`Project::open_raw` supports base, architecture, and entry, but CLI/MCP openers do not expose those settings. `Analysis::blocks_page` and `block_insns` already exist, whereas `Project::func_detail` serializes the whole function. Analysis documents missing indirect edges and heuristic function ownership; MCP tools reopen and rebuild the project on every call. Existing completed work, including LE support (`rsdbg-jix`) and human-readable IR coverage (`rsdbg-jbw.1`), must not be duplicated or reopened.

## Confirmed decisions

- Include all six proposed features and all three accompanying improvements.
- Prioritize raw mapping, bounded inspection, and diagnostics.
- Breaking CLI/MCP schemas are allowed, with explicit before/after migration documentation and regression tests. Permission is not a mandate to churn unrelated endpoints.
- Investigate indirect-control-flow recovery before selecting one implementation pattern.
- Only this plan and beads state are changed in plan mode. Implementation requires build mode.

## Assumptions and scope boundaries

- Continue as a headless, local, agent-first static analyzer; no GUI, dynamic execution, decompiler, symbolic executor, additional architecture, or new binary format in this roadmap.
- Preserve one JSON value on CLI stdout, existing exit-code conventions, hex/decimal address parsing, dual numeric/hex output addresses, and no writes to the analyzed binary.
- Proposed API/command names below are design targets; step 1 records the final schema contract before adapters are implemented.
- Explicit raw mapping is opt-in: CLI `--raw --arch ARCH --base ADDR [--entry ADDR]`; MCP optional `raw: {arch, base, entry?}` on binary-taking tools. Architecture and base are required in explicit raw mode; no flags preserves existing auto-detection/default fallback. Raw-only options without raw mode are errors. Accepted architectures match the existing five modes.
- A raw mapping is one contiguous existing `RawOptions` mapping, not a multi-segment firmware configuration language. Entry must be in the mapped range, with alignment appropriate to the selected mode; base-plus-length arithmetic is checked.
- Query pages retain the 1024-row maximum. New operation budgets below are initial explicit design limits, not claims about current constants.
- Annotation interchange is JSON returned by CLI/MCP and supplied as a bounded input document; no arbitrary server-side output-path writer is added. Shell redirection may save CLI output when the user executes the command in build mode.
- Import uses exact binary and mapping identity, with no force/rebase option in v1. Use a cryptographic digest for portable identity (SHA-256; a focused new dependency may be needed); the current 64-bit cache hash is not sufficient as an integrity check for interchange.
- Performance changes are conditional on measurements. No session cache, concurrency rewrite, or speedup promise is preapproved by this plan.
- Proprietary `_testdata/` binaries remain optional local oracles, never CI dependencies or tracked fixtures. Existing untracked `_testdata/` is left untouched.

## Plan

Each checkbox corresponds to exactly one beads issue. Each step is one logical change, including its directly associated tests. No implementation is done yet.

### 1. [small] Freeze the next JSON/CLI/MCP contract (P1)
- [ ] Define the feature schemas and deliberate breaking changes.
- **What/where:** update `docs/book/src/json-protocol.md` with page envelope `{total, offset, limit, next_offset, items}`, deterministic address ordering, zero-limit/end-of-list behavior, address encodings, input validation, and a protocol revision distinct from database schema and crate version. Document mappings for new CLI/MCP names in their reference chapters. Prefer one consistent page model for new views and intentionally revised function inspection; do not normalize unrelated strings/symbols endpoints just for style.
- **Why:** keep CLI and MCP consistent and prevent accidental breakage while changing large-function output. Exact counts describe the filtered result; `next_offset` is null when exhausted or limit is zero.
- **Verify:** schema examples cover empty, zero-limit, clipped-limit, and final pages; reviewed before steps 3, 5, 7, 10, or 12. Existing exit/error contracts remain explicit.

### 2. [medium] Make snapshot reuse mapping-aware (P1)
- [ ] Include effective loader configuration in cache identity.
- **What/where:** `src/db.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, and `src/loader.rs`: identity includes binary content, auto-versus-explicit-raw mode, raw arch/base/entry, and analysis revision. Validate before rebuilding cached layouts. Bump/migrate the sidecar schema as necessary. Same bytes with different options must never reuse layouts; no-options and explicit-raw opens must not accidentally alias.
- **Annotations:** preserve existing stale-content behavior for unchanged mapping, but reject reuse of a populated annotation sidecar under an incompatible mapping with an actionable separate-DB error. Do not silently move annotations to new addresses. Legacy snapshots whose mapping cannot be established are rebuilt, not trusted; ambiguous legacy raw annotations require a separate DB.
- **Why:** exposing `open_raw` broadly without this guard risks interpreting cached analysis with the wrong architecture or address space.
- **Verify:** new `tests/raw_mapping.rs` and `tests/stale_cache.rs` cases vary only architecture/base/entry/mode, test legacy handling, retain same-mapping annotation behavior, and assert reads never save or create sidecars.

### 3. [medium] Expose explicit raw mapping through both interfaces (P1)
- [ ] Thread validated raw options through every binary-taking operation.
- **What/where:** `src/cli.rs`, `src/mcp.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/loader.rs`: use the contract above and one shared validated opener/options parser rather than endpoint-specific interpretation. Respect default or explicit DB paths. Report effective mode, arch, base, and entry in project information.
- **Why:** support firmware/raw ARM/Thumb workflows using the engine already present.
- **Verify:** `tests/raw_mapping.rs`, `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/mcp.rs`: equivalent x86-32, AArch64, ARM32, and Thumb synthetic mappings give matching addresses; existing x86-64 mode remains covered. Test missing/unknown options, unmapped/misaligned entries, overflow, and unchanged no-flags container detection. Explicit raw mode must not fall back to a different mode after failure.
- **Depends on:** 1, 2.

### 4. [medium] Add bounded core function views (P1)
- [ ] Separate function summary, block pages, and instruction pages.
- **What/where:** `src/lib.rs`, existing helpers in `src/analysis.rs`, new `tests/function_pages.rs`: implement compact function metadata (entry/name/counts and call count, not unbounded call arrays), deterministic block summaries, and a paged block-instruction query. Resolve interior function addresses consistently; require the selected block to belong to that function. Avoid constructing the full function JSON before slicing.
- **Why:** existing internal page helpers can provide bounded responses without redesigning the engine.
- **Verify:** a synthetic function with more than 1024 instructions/pages reconstructs identically from successive pages, with no gaps/duplicates; limit zero/overflow-sized limit/out-of-range offsets behave as specified; unknown function/block reports NotFound. Per-page cloned/serialized rows scale with the selected page, not whole-function size.
- **Depends on:** 1.

### 5. [medium] Route CLI/MCP function inspection through bounded views (P1)
- [ ] Make compact `func` the default and expose `blocks` and `block_insns`.
- **What/where:** `src/cli.rs`, `src/mcp.rs`, `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/mcp.rs`: `func BINARY ADDR` returns compact metadata; `blocks BINARY ADDR --offset --limit` and `block-insns BINARY ADDR BLOCK --offset --limit` map to MCP `blocks`/`block_insns`. Keep full CFG export explicitly requested via existing `cfg`, rather than embedding it in `func`; document that CFG export can still be large.
- **Why:** a default tool call should not dump an entire large function. This is an intentional breaking response change; no hidden compatibility/full-output switch is required.
- **Verify:** CLI/MCP page values agree; `func` contains no instruction arrays; new tools appear in MCP discovery; large-function requests stay within row bounds; errors retain existing channel/exit semantics. Check byte-size sanity on the synthetic stress fixture without claiming row limits are a universal byte limit.
- **Depends on:** 3, 4.

### 6. [large] Capture and persist analysis diagnostics and discovery provenance (P1)
- [ ] Retain evidence about how analysis was obtained and where it is incomplete.
- **What/where:** `src/analysis.rs`, `src/disasm.rs` only if needed to retain typed control-flow facts, `src/db.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, new `tests/diagnostics.rs`: record discovery reasons (entry/export/direct-call/prologue), unresolved indirect jump/call sites, and decode failures encountered during discovery. Reasons can coexist and must be sorted/deduplicated. Provenance is evidence, not a fabricated confidence percentage or proof of correct boundaries.
- **Bounds/persistence:** cap diagnostic records at 100,000 per project; on diagnostic-cap exhaustion continue analysis and expose `diagnostics_truncated` plus omitted count. Existing hard analysis budgets still return Error::Limit rather than masquerading as successful partial analysis. Persist diagnostics/reasons with an analysis revision; old caches must reanalyze rather than manufacture a clean diagnostic set. Do not log every undecoded byte or build an unbounded event history.
- **Why:** callers need to distinguish known gaps, failed decodes, and heuristic seeds from verified analysis.
- **Verify:** synthetic direct/indirect/invalid/prologue cases produce exact reason/site records; valid termination is not a decode failure; deterministic fresh/cache round-trips agree; diagnostic-cap boundary behavior is explicit; tests assert unsupported control flow is not silently upgraded to a proven edge.
- **Depends on:** 2.

### 7. [medium] Expose paged diagnostics and provenance (P1)
- [ ] Add discoverable, bounded diagnostic queries and compact completeness metadata.
- **What/where:** `src/lib.rs`, `src/cli.rs`, `src/mcp.rs`, `tests/diagnostics.rs`, `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/mcp.rs`: `diagnostics` CLI/MCP query filtered by kind and optional containing function; use the page contract. Add reason sets to compact function metadata, and diagnostic totals/truncation/analysis revision to project info. Do not equate zero retained diagnostics with proof of complete recovery.
- **Why:** make the engine's limitations actionable without flooding each normal tool response.
- **Verify:** filtering precedes pagination; CLI/MCP return identical records; reasons survive rename and snapshot reopen; invalid filters are errors; querying does not write a sidecar.
- **Depends on:** 1, 5, 6.

### 8. [medium] Publish machine-readable IR coverage (P2)
- [ ] Distinguish implemented lift mappings from semantic completeness.
- **What/where:** `src/ir.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/cli.rs`, `src/mcp.rs`, `tests/ir.rs`, `tests/addr_hex.rs`: add an `ir_coverage` library query and CLI `ir-coverage`/MCP `ir_coverage` accepting architecture without opening a binary. Return implemented opcode families, explicit unknown/partial status, and limitations (operand strings, flags, stack/calling-convention effects, no SSA/PHI production). Add per-range counts for decoded/lifted/unlifted instructions based on actual lift results and a bounded mnemonic summary.
- **Why:** extends completed human-readable coverage work (`rsdbg-jbw.1`), rather than duplicating it or claiming decompiler semantics. Real NOP and unlifted fallback NOP must remain distinguishable.
- **Verify:** tests cover genuine NOP versus fallback warning, mapped-but-partial semantics, all five modes, and consistency between advertised families and representative positive/negative lifts. No second drifting list of individually supported mnemonics if family dispatch can share metadata.
- **Depends on:** 1.

### 9. [medium] Implement bounded byte-pattern search in the core (P2)
- [ ] Search mapped, file-backed bytes using literal bytes and `??` wildcards.
- **What/where:** new `src/search.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, new `tests/byte_search.rs`: parse whitespace-separated full-byte tokens (e.g. `48 8B ?? ??`), reject empty/all-wildcard/odd/invalid patterns, and cap pattern length at 4096 bytes. Support section and half-open VA-range filters; return VA/hex, file offset where available, section, and match length. Include overlapping matches, use stable VA ordering, and never bridge gaps or separate mappings; suppress duplicate representations of the same match in overlapping section views.
- **Bounds:** scan at most 256 MiB of unique file-backed mapped bytes per request, with explicit Error::Limit rather than silent truncation. Do not materialize virtual BSS. Cap result pages at 1024 and skip/materialize matches lazily; an exact total may require a full bounded scan. Use a literal anchor plus verification instead of expanding wildcards to regex or an accidental unbounded quadratic scan.
- **Why:** support locating instruction signatures and binary structures without adding execution or patching.
- **Verify:** literal/wildcard/overlap/page-boundary matches, filters, raw mapping, invalid tokens, BSS/gap behavior, arithmetic bounds, and budget edges. Compare against a simple bounded reference matcher over randomized small buffers.
- **Depends on:** 1, 2.

### 10. [small] Expose byte search in CLI/MCP (P2)
- [ ] Add `search-bytes` / `search_bytes` with shared filters and page envelopes.
- **What/where:** `src/cli.rs`, `src/mcp.rs`, `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/mcp.rs`: pattern, section, range start/end, offset/limit, and common raw/DB options. No regex/nibble wildcard language, external signature database, or file-writing result export.
- **Why:** make the core search useful from both supported interfaces.
- **Verify:** exact CLI/MCP parity on synthetic PE/raw patterns; malformed patterns and unmapped ranges return documented errors; repeated queries never create/write sidecars; discoverability schema includes all filters.
- **Depends on:** 3, 9.

### 11. [medium] Add validated, atomic annotation interchange (P2)
- [ ] Define versioned JSON export and all-or-nothing import.
- **What/where:** new `src/annotations.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/db.rs`, `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` if SHA-256 support is added, new `tests/annotation_transfer.rs`: export format revision, SHA-256, binary length, effective mapping, and sorted nonempty `{addr, rename?, comment?}` rows. Exclude host paths and analysis snapshots. Import validates the entire document before one write transaction; rename targets must be known entries, comments retain the any-address contract. Reuse field/row/storage caps; cap serialized interchange documents at 16 MiB in both directions, reject duplicate addresses, malformed identity, and unsupported revisions. Oversized export fails explicitly rather than emitting a document the importer cannot accept or silently truncating annotations.
- **Merge policy:** default fails on differing existing field values; equal values are idempotent. Explicit `overwrite` replaces supplied fields only; absent fields leave existing values unchanged; empty strings clear supplied fields. Untouched annotations remain. Whole-set replace/rebase/force import is out of scope.
- **Why:** preserve valuable analyst work independently of the disposable analysis cache without partial imports or cross-binary corruption.
- **Verify:** export/import/reopen round-trip, exact identity mismatch, raw mapping mismatch, duplicate rows, oversized input/text, unknown rename, comments outside mapped memory, conflict/overwrite/clear semantics, idempotence, and failure in the last row leaving DB and in-memory annotations unchanged. Export is read-only.
- **Depends on:** 2.

### 12. [medium] Expose portable annotations through CLI/MCP (P2)
- [ ] Add export/import operations without arbitrary server-side output paths.
- **What/where:** `src/cli.rs`, `src/mcp.rs`, `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/mcp.rs`: CLI `annotations-export BINARY` emits one JSON document; `annotations-import BINARY --input PATH [--overwrite]` reads capped JSON and returns counts. MCP `annotations_export` returns the document and `annotations_import` accepts the document plus optional overwrite. Common binary/raw/DB options apply. Enforce MCP serialized document/row/text limits before transaction; check rmcp input-allocation limitations and document any transport-level residual risk.
- **Why:** support backups/sharing while keeping analyzed binaries immutable and stdout machine-readable.
- **Verify:** CLI export can be imported into a fresh DB; MCP equivalent produces the same annotations; invalid final row/conflict yields no partial write; tool schemas, runtime error behavior, and hash/mapping validation match the core.
- **Depends on:** 1, 3, 11.

### 13. [medium] Benchmark repeated MCP investigation workflows (P2)
- [ ] Establish reproducible costs before choosing an optimization.
- **What/where:** new `tests/mcp_workflow_perf.rs` (ignored/manual measurements, not flaky timing gates), new `docs/book/src/performance.md`, `docs/book/src/SUMMARY.md`: deterministic synthetic small and large fixtures, cold/no-sidecar, saved-sidecar/new-process, and repeated same-process scenarios. Measure `project_info → functions → func → blocks → block_insns → xrefs → strings`, with fixture size/counts, compiler/platform, wall time distribution, response bytes, and peak RSS where available. Separate file read/hash, layout replay, analysis, and serialization using minimal measurement hooks only if external measurements cannot isolate them.
- **Why:** cache-hit opens still replay layouts, but the dominant cost and useful optimization are not yet established. Do not assume page-cache-warm equals in-memory-project reuse.
- **Verify:** release-build run command is documented; at least five measured repetitions after warm-up; fresh and cached functional outputs agree; no claimed speedup without before/after data; measurements and tool availability limitations are recorded, not encoded as arbitrary CI deadlines.
- **Depends on:** 5 (the workflow uses new bounded tools).

### 14. [small] Decide the smallest justified MCP optimization (P2)
- [ ] Record a go/no-go decision from step 13 rather than prebuilding a cache.
- **What/where:** update the performance chapter and this plan with the measured bottleneck and proposed bounded solution, or explicitly conclude no optimization is justified. If a resident-project cache is proposed, specify eviction/memory budget, binary+mapping identity, external annotation invalidation, rename/comment coherence, DB lock lifecycle, and runtime/cancellation behavior before an implementation issue is approved. A raw-size or mtime-only cache key is insufficient.
- **Why:** avoid trading correctness, memory bounds, and cross-process freshness for unproven speed.
- **Verify:** decision cites reproducible measurements and unchanged observable results; any proposed implementation has quantified acceptance criteria and a separate follow-up issue. This task is complete with a justified no-go; this roadmap does not promise an optimization implementation.
- **Depends on:** 13.

### 15. [medium] Investigate one conservative jump-table pattern (P3)
- [ ] Establish whether one indirect jump can be resolved with bounded evidence.
- **What/where:** read `src/disasm.rs`, `src/analysis.rs`, `src/ir.rs`, and loader mappings; record findings and an exact implementation design in this plan. Use synthetic x86-32/x86-64 pattern candidates first; inspect LE fixup/address limitations without assuming relocated table entries. Select exactly one pattern only if bounds checks, table base, entry width, target executable mapping, and branch semantics can be established from typed decoder facts.
- **Deliverable:** positive and near-miss byte layouts, explicit rejection conditions, maximum 1024 entries/site and 100,000 recovered edges/project as initial caps, direct-versus-inferred provenance, serialization/revision changes, and expected CFG/xref/function-ownership effects. No decoder-text regex inference, whole-memory pointer guessing, or general symbolic execution.
- **Why:** the current known gap is real, but a broad recovery promise would be unsafe and hard to verify.
- **Verify:** design explains every proposed edge and at least five false-positive cases (missing guard, invalid base/width, non-executable target, truncated table, unsupported relocation); record go/no-go. A no-go leaves step 16 blocked/deferred, not implemented speculatively.
- **Depends on:** 6, 8.

### 16. [large] Implement only the proven indirect-jump pattern, conditional on go (P3)
- [ ] Add the approved bounded resolver, or defer after a no-go investigation.
- **What/where:** `src/disasm.rs`, `src/analysis.rs`, `src/db.rs`, new `tests/jump_tables.rs`; `src/lib.rs`/adapters only for agreed evidence fields. Require the exact prerequisites from step 15, keep direct/inferred edge evidence distinct, retain unresolved diagnostics when prerequisites fail, integrate cache replay/revision invalidation, and never modify segment bytes or the original file.
- **Why:** improve CFG completeness without silently inventing control flow. Shared-tail/function ownership limitations remain explicit.
- **Verify:** exact recovered edge/xref sets on the approved positive fixture; every near-miss is unresolved; table/project caps cannot OOM or silently clip inferred graphs (report an explicit diagnostic and leave the site unresolved); fresh/snapshot queries agree; existing direct-flow behavior is unchanged.
- **Depends on:** 7, 15, and a recorded go decision. Priority remains P3; do not count a deliberate deferral as implemented.

### 17. [medium] Publish migration guidance and verify the integrated release (P2)
- [ ] Document delivered features and run the complete configured gate.
- **What/where:** `README.md`, `docs/book/src/cli-reference.md`, `mcp-tools.md`, `json-protocol.md`, `sidecar-format.md`, `architecture.md`, `performance.md`, and `SUMMARY.md` as needed: examples, new tool count/schema revision, old/new `func` response, raw mapping/cache behavior, diagnostic/IR limitations, pattern syntax, annotation conflict policy, and legacy sidecar handling. Do not write user documentation as a history of planning tasks. Update release notes via the established release-plz workflow, not an invented manual version bump.
- **Verify:** run, in order, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo doc --no-deps`; documentation must be warning-free. Run `mdbook build docs/book` in build mode and the manual release workflow benchmark. CLI/MCP capability discovery and examples match executable behavior; no proprietary inputs or sidecars enter tracked files.
- **Depends on:** 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14. If step 16 ships in this release, include its tests/docs; otherwise explicitly list it as deferred and do not block the primary release on research.

## Ordering and parallelism

- Start with 1 and 2 in parallel; 4 follows 1. Prioritize 3, 5, 6, and 7 before P2 feature work.
- After the foundation, IR coverage (8), search (9–10), and annotation transfer (11–12) can proceed independently; coordinate shared CLI/MCP and DB files to avoid conflicts.
- Performance 13→14 follows bounded inspection. Research 15→conditional 16 follows diagnostics/IR and is not a blocker for the main release.
- 17 is the integration/documentation release gate. Each feature issue owns its tests; 17 is not a late testing phase.

## Files

These are expected build-mode changes, not changes made during this planning session.

- **Modify:** `src/lib.rs`, `src/loader.rs`, `src/analysis.rs`, `src/db.rs`, `src/disasm.rs` (diagnostic/indirect facts only as needed), `src/ir.rs`, `src/cli.rs`, `src/mcp.rs`; `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` (only if a digest dependency is needed); `tests/stale_cache.rs`, `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/mcp.rs`, `tests/ir.rs`, `tests/addr_hex.rs`, `tests/common/mod.rs` and `tests/fixtures/builders.rs` only for focused fixture support; `README.md`; existing book chapters listed above.
- **Create:** `src/search.rs`, `src/annotations.rs`, `tests/raw_mapping.rs`, `tests/function_pages.rs`, `tests/diagnostics.rs`, `tests/byte_search.rs`, `tests/annotation_transfer.rs`, `tests/mcp_workflow_perf.rs`, `docs/book/src/performance.md`; conditional `tests/jump_tables.rs` after a research go decision.
- **Delete:** none.
- **Keep unchanged:** original analyzed binaries, proprietary `_testdata/`, release automation/CI policy unless a demonstrated integration requirement emerges. No general module split or adjacent refactor.

## Risks

1. **Wrong cache identity or stale annotations:** raw remapping and richer snapshots can mix incompatible address spaces. Guard loader configuration before replay, reject ambiguous mapping changes with annotations, and test legacy sidecars explicitly.
2. **Oversized/untrusted inputs or misleading completeness:** annotation JSON, wildcard scans, diagnostic records, and inferred edges need independent budgets and truthful errors/truncation metadata. Row pagination alone does not bound every transport allocation or CFG export.
3. **False analysis claims and scope creep:** diagnostic absence is not proof; IR mappings are partial; inferred edges require evidence. Benchmark/research decisions may legitimately yield no-go. Do not turn either into a general decompiler or session framework.

## Alternatives considered

- **Expose raw flags first and fix cache identity later** — rejected because the same bytes opened with different architecture/base can reuse incompatible layouts or annotations.
- **Build a resident MCP cache and broad jump-table resolver immediately** — rejected because measured bottlenecks and a reliable conservative pattern are not established. Separate evidence-gathering from conditional implementation.

## Success criteria

- [x] All nine approved proposal areas have detailed issues, concrete acceptance checks, priorities, and dependency ordering; conditional work is clearly marked.
- [ ] Same bytes under different raw mappings never reuse incompatible cached analysis; mapping-mismatched annotation reuse fails without mutation.
- [ ] CLI/MCP raw opens report matching effective architecture/base/entry; defaults remain unchanged.
- [ ] Large-function block/instruction pages reconstruct the exact original sequence within 1024-row page caps; default `func` remains compact.
- [ ] Discovery reasons and diagnostic sites are deterministic, bounded, filterable, and identical after valid snapshot reuse; missing diagnostics are not represented as proof of completeness.
- [ ] IR metadata distinguishes genuine NOP, partial implemented mappings, and unlifted fallback; all five modes have coverage checks.
- [ ] Byte search returns exact overlapping fixture matches and correct offsets without crossing gaps, allocating BSS, or silently exceeding scan limits.
- [ ] Annotation export/import is versioned, identity-checked, bounded, idempotent, and atomic even when the final row fails validation.
- [ ] Repeated-MCP benchmark results and a measured optimization go/no-go are recorded; no unsupported speedup claim.
- [ ] Jump-table investigation records go/no-go; if implemented, every inferred edge is justified and negative fixtures remain unresolved.
- [ ] Breaking response changes and legacy sidecar behavior have tested, executable migration examples.
- [ ] `cargo test` passes; then `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and warning-free `cargo doc --no-deps` pass.
- [ ] `mdbook build docs/book` succeeds in build mode; no analyzed binary, proprietary fixture, or sidecar is committed.

title: MCP: stateless per-call open + no save -> full re-analysis on every tool call; global lock blocks runtime
description:
## Problem
- Every tool calls `open()` → `crate::open_mapped` ([src/mcp.rs:35-54](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/mcp.rs#L35-L54)). Each call re-reads the file, computes FNV + SHA-256, decodes every redb JSON row and re-disassembles every instruction (`rebuild`, [src/analysis.rs:1097-1208](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L1097-L1208)).
- No MCP tool calls `save()`; only rename/comment fall back to a full save (`project_info` is read-only, [src/mcp.rs:513-523](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/mcp.rs#L513-L523)). Unless someone ran CLI `load` first, **every MCP call runs the full `analyze()`**: about 1.3 s for a 6.5 MB Mach-O, 18 s for the 40k-jump-site raw blob (see the resolve_indirect_jumps issue).
- One global `Arc<Mutex<()>>` serialises all calls ([src/mcp.rs:484-486](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/mcp.rs#L484-L486)), and the synchronous tool bodies run on tokio worker threads (they should use `spawn_blocking`).
- The no-go decision in docs/performance.md (rsdbg-0vt.14) was measured on fixtures of 3.9 KB or less.

## Fix (staged)
1. **Cheap:** after a cache miss or stale result in MCP, call `save()`, or add a `load` MCP tool for parity with the CLI (see the parity issue in the feature epic).
2. Keep a small in-process LRU (e.g. 4 entries) of `Project` keyed by `(canonical path, db path, mapping, fat_arch)` and validated by `(len, mtime)`, re-hashing only when those change. redb allows one handle per file per process, so the cache must own the handle or reopen it under the lock.
3. Run tool bodies in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. Consider a per-project lock instead of the global one.

## Acceptance
On a multi-MB binary, the second `functions` call through MCP is at least 10× faster than the first. Update docs/performance.md with real-size numbers.
close_reason: Merged: 4-entry MCP project LRU with per-sidecar locks, async spawn_blocking tools, new load tool; second functions call ~4600x faster (release) on 2.9MB blob. Full gate green on master.

title: Xref queries: two full linear scans per request; no to-index; slice_to rebuilds HashMap
description:
## Problem
- [src/lib.rs:1594-1610](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L1594-L1610) `xrefs_matching`: linear filter over all xrefs (up to 3M). `query_xrefs` and `count_xrefs` ([src/lib.rs:~1581](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L1581), [src/lib.rs:~1592](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L1592)) each run it, so every request does 2 full passes even with `--from`/`--to`.
- Same in `Analysis::xrefs_to` / `xrefs_from` ([src/analysis.rs:1437-1453](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L1437-L1453)).
- `slice_to` ([src/analysis.rs:797-869](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L797-L869)) builds a `HashMap` over all xrefs on every call. `insn_preds` collects a `Vec` of block addresses per BFS node (~L853).

## Fix
- `from`: binary search (xrefs are sorted `(from, kind, to)`).
- `to`: a secondary `Vec<u32>` index sorted by `to`, built once after load (lazily via `OnceCell`).
- Count and page in one pass.
- Make `slice_to` use the `to` index, and use `position` directly on `block.insns`.

## Acceptance
Results unchanged (tests/paged_queries.rs). `xrefs --to X` on the reference binary takes under 5 ms after open.
close_reason: Merged to master: binary search + lazy to-index, single-pass count/page; gate green (694 passed)

title: Linear lookups on hot paths: containing_function, inferred-pair owner, layout inferred_edges, seg_at
description:
Same pattern in four places: a linear scan where an ordered lookup already exists.

1. **`containing_function`**, [src/analysis.rs:721-727](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L721-L727): `func.blocks.values().any(..)` is O(B_f). It is called per diagnostic in `diagnostics_matching` ([src/analysis.rs:~1476](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L1476)), per row in `query_diagnostics` ([src/lib.rs:~1752](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L1752)), per BFS node in `insn_preds` (~L839) and per row in `slice_page`. Fix: `func.blocks.range(..=va).next_back().filter(|(_, b)| va < b.end())`, which `insn_preds` already does at ~L845.
2. **Owner of each inferred pair**, [src/analysis.rs:2718-2734](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L2718-L2734): for each pair it loops over **all functions**. O(P × F × log B) with up to 100k pairs. Fix: `function_owner(&entries, site)` then one `blocks.range` lookup, or a global block-start map like `block_func`.
3. **`layout`**, [src/analysis.rs:1051-1056](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L1051-L1056): `f.inferred_edges()` collects the full set for every block (O(B_f × I_f)). The budget check in [src/db.rs:725-729](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/db.rs#L725-L729) allocates just to call `.len()`. Fix: `inferred.range((b.start, 0)..=(b.start, u64::MAX))` plus an `inferred_len()` method.
4. **`AddrSpace::seg_at`**, [src/analysis.rs:1676-1680](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L1676-L1680): linear over up to 256 segments **per decode**, in both analyze and rebuild. Fix: sort by vaddr and use `partition_point`.
5. **`round1`** ([src/analysis.rs:~2541](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L2541)) copies every decoded key into a new `BTreeSet`; use `walk.decoded.contains_key` instead.

Note: fixing (1) with `range` also touches the ownership-consistency correctness issue (rsdbg-zvm.16); do those together.
close_reason: Fix already in master via b949d6b (ordered lookups); added 94b93d3 regression test ordered_lookup_helpers_match_collecting_predecessors pinning inferred_succs/inferred_len/containing_function. Full gate green.

title: Byte scanning: x86 prologue scan ~11 ns/byte; byte-search anchors on first literal, not rarest
description:
## 1. Prologue candidate scan
`CandStream::match_at` ([src/analysis.rs:1970-2012](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L1970-L2012)) slices and compares 4 patterns at **every byte** on x86. Measured on a 250 MB raw blob of `c3`: 3.62 s on x86_64 versus 0.74 s on aarch64 (word stride), so about 2.9 s in the scan (≈ 0.6 s per 50 MB of `.text`).
Fix: jump between candidates with `memchr::memchr2(0x48, 0xF3)` (x86-64) or `memchr3(0x89, 0x83, 0x81)` (x86-32), or a 256-entry first-byte table, and verify only at hits. `memchr` is already a transitive dependency; check deny.toml.

## 2. search-bytes anchor
[src/search.rs:188-192](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/search.rs#L188-L192), [src/search.rs:~283](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/search.rs#L283): the anchor is the **first** literal byte and the search uses `iter().position` (not memchr). A pattern starting with `00`, `ff`, `cc` or `c3` verifies at almost every offset; `c3 c3 c3 90` on the 250 MB blob added about 0.9 s.
Fix: choose the rarest literal using a static byte-frequency table, or use `memchr::memmem` on the longest literal run, then verify the wildcards around it.

## Acceptance
Identical candidates and hits (existing tests/byte_search.rs and analysis tests). The 250 MB `c3` blob on x86_64 takes under 1.5 s.
close_reason: Merged to master (50d60ab via work/5tk.12 + merge): memchr-anchored scan, identical output, gate green

title: resolve_indirect_jumps: O(J*D) rescan of diagnostics; 40k jump sites = 18 s (cheap DoS)
description:
## Problem
[src/analysis.rs:2400-2418](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L2400-L2418):
```rust
while let Some(site) = walk.diagnostics.iter()
    .filter(|d| d.kind == UnresolvedIndirectJump && !processed.contains(&d.addr))
    .map(|d| d.addr).next() { processed.insert(site); ... }
```
Each pass scans all diagnostics from the start, so the cost is O(J × D). This runs for **every format and arch**, even though the resolvers return `None` right away unless the format is Raw ([src/analysis.rs:2214](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L2214)).

## Measured (release, raw x86_64 blobs of `55 48 89 e5 ff e0`)
| sites | time |
|---|---|
| 10k | 1.4 s |
| 20k | 5.75 s |
| 40k | 18.0 s |

A control blob with `ret` or `call rax` in the same position takes 0.15–0.20 s. An ELF or PE full of `jmp reg` takes the same path. Real C++/Go binaries with many indirect jumps pay for this too.

## Fix
1. Return early when the resolvers can't apply (`format != Raw` or arch not x86). Make this a single predicate shared with the resolver gate so they can't drift apart.
2. Otherwise use a worklist: collect the initial sites into a `BTreeSet`, `pop_first`, and after each `Walker::run` scan only the diagnostics appended since the last cursor (`walk.diagnostics[cursor..]`).

## Test
Add a scaling test to tests/input_budgets.rs or tests/jump_tables.rs: 20k sites finish in under 1 s in release (or assert the visit count via a debug counter, so the test doesn't depend on timing). Existing jump_tables tests must still pass.
close_reason: Shared indirect_slot_width gate + early return for non-raw/non-x86; Walker::run returns fresh sites feeding a BTreeSet worklist (pop_first). New many_register_indirect_sites_visit_once_each scaling test (20k sites) + all 26 jump_tables tests pass; clippy/fmt/doc clean.

title: Staged open: loader-only commands still rebuild full analysis on every CLI call
description:
## Problem
`open_inner` ([src/lib.rs:483-533](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L483-L533)) always produces a full `Analysis`. On a cache hit it runs `rebuild` ([src/analysis.rs:1097-1208](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L1097-L1208)), which re-decodes and formats every instruction. Commands that need only the loader output or counts pay for that anyway: `sections`, `symbols`, `search-bytes`, `strings` (partly), `annotations-export`, `stats`, `project_info`.

Measured: 0.42 s / 403 MB RSS per `stats` on a 6.5 MB Mach-O (cache hit).

## Fix
- `Project::open_loader_only` (or lazy analysis via `OnceCell<Analysis>`) for loader-only commands.
- `stats` / `project_info` counts read from the stored metadata.
- Later: decode instructions per block on first access (`OnceCell` per block, or `Project::insns_of(block)`), so `func` / `block-insns` decode only what they render.

## Acceptance
On a multi-MB binary with a sidecar, `sections` and `symbols` take under 50 ms, and the JSON output is unchanged (golden comparison in tests/cli.rs).
close_reason: Merged: LoaderProject hit-only view; sections/symbols/stats ~17ms cache-hit (was 0.42s), RSS 81->27MB. Golden test over 11 commands. Full gate green on integrated branch.

title: Insn is heavy (~1.2 KB/insn): per-decode IntelFormatter, string ops, Pass B clones all insns
description:
## Problem
- `Insn` holds `mnem: String`, `ops: Vec<String>`, `bytes` and text. Measured cost is about 1.2 KB RSS per instruction, so about 1.2 GB at `MAX_TOTAL_INSNS` (1M).
- [src/disasm.rs:594](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/disasm.rs#L594): `IntelFormatter::new()` on **every** x86 decode.
- [src/disasm.rs:481-551](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/disasm.rs#L481-L551) and [src/disasm.rs:571-646](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/disasm.rs#L571-L646): format → lowercase → split → `masm_to_hex` / `masm_word`, all allocating per word.
- [src/analysis.rs:2663](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L2663): Pass B `cur.push(d.insn.clone())` while `decoded` stays alive through Pass D, so peak memory holds 2× every instruction.

## Fix (incremental)
1. Reuse one formatter (a field on the decoder context, or `thread_local!`).
2. In Pass B, move instructions out of `decoded` (`BTreeMap::remove` or `std::mem::take`), and keep a slim `(flow, mem_target, table_base)` map for Passes C and D.
3. Longer term: a compact instruction record (addr, size, flow, branch_target, mem_target, table_base), formatting text only when rendering a page. Must keep the IR lift working (it lifts from strings today; see the structured-IR feature issue).

## Acceptance
Peak RSS for a fresh `load` of the 6.5 MB reference binary drops from 760 MB by at least 40%, and the output is identical.
close_reason: Merged work/5tk4: thread-local formatter/scratch reuse in disasm_first_x86; decode_stability regression tests; Pass-B drain measured +11% RSS and deliberately reverted, documented in commit

title: diff: O(F*X) fingerprint xref scan + O(A*B) fuzzy pass with retain
description:
## Problem
1. [src/diff.rs:305-316](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/diff.rs#L305-L316): for each function, scan **all** xrefs to count in/out. That is O(F × X) per side, about 10¹¹ steps at 100k functions and 1M xrefs. Measured: a 6.5 MB Mach-O against a 0.5 MB LE took 1.44 s, about 0.8 s of it in diff.
2. [src/diff.rs:431-452](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/diff.rs#L431-L452): the fuzzy pass compares every remaining A against every remaining B, plus `rest_b.retain(..)` at O(n) per match. About 10¹⁰ comparisons for two poorly matching 100k-function builds. Combined with the MCP global lock, one `diff` call stalls the whole server.

## Fix
1. Xrefs are stored sorted by `from`, so count out-refs with two `partition_point` calls per function range. Build a sorted `Vec<u64>` of `to` once and count in-refs the same way. That gives O((F + X) log X).
2. Bucket `rest_b` in a `HashMap<(calls_out, callers_in, xrefs_out, xrefs_in), Vec<usize>>` (the exact-equality gate already used) and compare only within a bucket. Use the existing `used_b` instead of `retain`.

## Acceptance
Diff output is identical on the existing tests/ diff fixtures. A synthetic 20k-function pair finishes in under 1 s.
close_reason: Implemented on work/5tk.5 (60a995a): partition_point xref counts + bucketed fuzzy pass; 9 diff integration + 5 lib tests pass, clippy/fmt clean, 77ms release on 20k-pair acceptance

title: load rewrites all tables even on cache hit; sidecar grows (134->269 MB) without compaction
description:
## Problem
- CLI `load` always calls `p.save()` ([src/cli.rs:582-591](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/cli.rs#L582-L591)) → `db::save` ([src/db.rs:~1055](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/db.rs#L1055)), which deletes and rewrites all 8 tables, even when `open_inner` just took the cache-hit path with identical metadata.
- Measured on the 6.5 MB Mach-O: repeat `load` takes 1.1–1.6 s each, and the sidecar went from 134 MB to 269 MB, then 167 MB (redb free pages are not compacted).

## Fix
- `open_inner` reports whether the snapshot was a fresh hit; `load` skips `save` when it was and the metadata is equal.
- After a full rewrite, call `Database::compact()` (the existing `compact_db` / `db vacuum` helper from rsdbg-jbw.3) or do so when the free ratio passes a threshold.

## Acceptance
Repeat `load` on an unchanged binary takes under 0.5 s and leaves the sidecar size unchanged (test in tests/stale_cache.rs asserting the file size is stable across 3 loads).
close_reason: Merged to master (fabbb95 via work/5tk.6): skip save on fresh snapshot, compact after rewrite, gate green

title: classify() runs full IR lift per instruction (alloc + ~600-mnemonic linear scans)
description:
## Problem
[src/analysis.rs:1631-1633](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L1631-L1633): `classify(arch, insn)` = `crate::ir::lift(arch, insn).first()...`. Called per decoded instruction in `Walker::run`, again in Pass C ([src/analysis.rs:~2760](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L2760)) and in `structure()`. Each call:
- allocates a `Vec<IrInsn>` and clones operand strings;
- walks a chain of `slice::contains` over about 600 x86 mnemonic tables ([src/ir.rs:~390](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/ir.rs#L390), [src/ir.rs:~924](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/ir.rs#L924)); control-flow mnemonics are checked after about 500 comparisons;
- formats a warning String for unmapped mnemonics ([src/ir.rs:~1231](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/ir.rs#L1231)).

## Fix
- `fn flow_of(arch, &Insn) -> Flow` with no allocation: x86 can use iced's `FlowControl` (store it on `Insn` at decode time); ARM can match the branch/return mnemonics first.
- Pass C reuses `decoded[&last.addr].flow` instead of lifting again.
- Optional: turn the IR tables into `match` or a phf map.

## Acceptance
Flow results are identical (add a property test over the existing fixtures comparing `flow_of` with `classify`). Analysis time on the reference binary drops measurably.
close_reason: Merged to master: ir::control_op + flow_of, ~2.5x analyze speedup; gate green

title: Sidecar ~20x binary size: JSON rows, format!() keys, hex twins, per-insn JSON layouts
description:
## Problem
134 MB sidecar for a 6.5 MB input.
- Every row is JSON ([src/db.rs:72-79](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/db.rs#L72-L79), [src/db.rs:648-663](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/db.rs#L648-L663)); keys are `format!`-built strings.
- Xref and string rows store the `*_hex` twins because storage reuses the wire `Serialize` ([src/analysis.rs:144-157](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L144-L157)) — [src/db.rs:~1137](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/db.rs#L1137), [src/db.rs:~1147](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/db.rs#L1147).
- Each instruction layout is stored as a JSON object (`{"addr":…,"size":…}`, about 28 B for about 1 B of real information).

Decoding all of this is a large share of the 0.42 s cache-hit open.

## Fix
Binary encoding (postcard or bincode; check `deny.toml` licenses) with tuple or `u64` big-endian keys. Store blocks as `(start, end, Vec<u8> insn_sizes)`. Use a storage-only serde struct without hex twins. Bump `ANALYSIS_REVISION` / the schema version. Old sidecars become stale, which the existing stale-path handling already covers.

## Acceptance
Sidecar under 3× the binary on the reference input, cache-hit open at least 2× faster, all stale_cache/annotation tests pass.
close_reason: Merged to master; all gates green

title: Open hashes byte-at-a-time FNV + eager SHA-256 and holds input 3x (Vec, Segment.data, Section.data); memmap2 unused
description:
## Problem
- [src/lib.rs:474](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L474): byte-at-a-time FNV-1a over the whole input on every open; [src/lib.rs:526](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L526), [src/lib.rs:587](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L587): eager SHA-256 (only needed for annotation export/import identity).
- [src/db.rs:86-95](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/db.rs#L86-L95): hash helpers.
- [src/lib.rs:1931-1975](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L1931-L1975): read into a `Vec`, and `reserve_exact(n)` per 64 KiB chunk at [src/lib.rs:1970](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L1970) prevents amortised growth (up to 8,192 reallocations at the 512 MiB cap).
- [src/loader.rs:~484](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/loader.rs#L484), [src/loader.rs:~520](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/loader.rs#L520): bytes copied into `Segment.data` and again into `Section.data`, up to 3× the file size resident.
- `memmap2` is listed in Cargo.toml but not used.

## Fix
- SHA-256 in `OnceCell`, computed on first use.
- Replace FNV with xxh3-64/128 (or blake3) for the content key. Coordinate with the snapshot-identity correctness issue (rsdbg-zvm.12).
- `Vec::with_capacity(len.min(cap))` once, or mmap (memmap2 is already a dependency; the input must not be mutated, read-only map).
- `Section` refers to a file range or offset into the segment instead of an owned `Vec<u8>`.
- Or remove the unused `memmap2` dependency.

## Acceptance
Open of a 100 MB raw blob: RSS about 1× the input, and hash time under 50 ms.
close_reason: Done: lazy SHA-256, xxh3 content hash, single-alloc/mmap-free open, metadata-only Sections; 100MB raw 1.02x RSS, hash 3.4ms; merged to master

title: Project review 2026-10-17: missing features and parity gaps
description: Gap analysis from the 2026-10-17 project review at commit c1bd143: what an agent doing RE (malware triage, crackmes, firmware, patch diffing) needs compared with Ghidra/IDA/Binja/rizin headless. Ordered by agent value over effort. Note: Ghidra CSV/XML interop (rsdbg-ljy.9) was declined earlier and is not proposed again. Respect the contracts: never write the analyzed binary; one JSON value per CLI command; bounded/paged output.

title: Use object symbol tables (local/static funcs) for names and discovery seeds
description:
## Gap
`load_object` reads only `file.imports()` and `file.exports()` ([src/loader.rs:532-575](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/loader.rs#L532-L575)). Nothing calls `object::Object::symbols()` / `dynamic_symbols()`. Function names come only from exports and Mach-O stubs ([src/analysis.rs:2672-2682](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L2672-L2682)); seeds only from entry, exports and stubs ([src/analysis.rs:1749-1780](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L1749-L1780)).

## Why
Unstripped ELF/PE (with COFF symtab)/Mach-O/`.o` files lose every local or static function name and boundary. That covers most crackmes, CTF binaries, debug builds and object files. It is the top agent-value gap.

## Approach (S)
- Collect defined `SymbolKind::Text` symbols in executable sections, deduplicated by address, capped (new `MAX_SYMBOLS`, counted in the metadata budget).
- New `DiscoveryReason::Symbol`; seed them in `authoritative_seeds`; name precedence: rename > export > symbol > stub > `func@`.
- Mask the Thumb bit for ARM (see rsdbg-zvm.6).
- Expose them in `symbols` output (`locals` array or a `kind` field).
- Bump `ANALYSIS_REVISION`. Update the JSON protocol doc.

## Test
Synthetic ELF/COFF fixture with a static function that is not called from entry → discovered and named.
close_reason: Merged: SymbolRef/MAX_SYMBOLS/canonical_code_addr in loader, DiscoveryReason::Symbol seeding, export>symbol>stub precedence, ANALYSIS_REVISION 6, 6 new tests. Full gate green on master.

title: Noreturn call handling (exit/abort/__stack_chk_fail/ExitProcess + propagation)
description:
## Gap
Every call adds a fall-through CFG edge ([src/analysis.rs:2781-2789](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L2781-L2789)). Code after `exit`, `abort`, `__assert_fail`, `__stack_chk_fail`, `ExitProcess`, `_Unwind_Resume`, `__cxa_throw` and similar is treated as reachable. The walker decodes padding or data as code, producing bogus blocks and merged functions.

## Approach (M)
1. Static list of known noreturn import names (glibc, msvcrt, kernel32, libSystem).
2. Mark calls to them (requires import call-site naming, see the import-naming issue) → no fall-through edge.
3. Propagate: a function with no Return-reachable exit is noreturn; iterate to a fixpoint (bounded).
4. Expose `noreturn: bool` on function rows; diagnostic on the cut edge.
close_reason: Implemented: noreturn list + fixpoint propagation + cut edges, tests/noreturn.rs; merged to master

title: User-defined function seeds (define/undefine) persisted in the sidecar
description:
## Gap
Rename and comment are the only writes. Agents can't say "there is code at 0x1234" (shellcode, firmware vector tables, obfuscated code, missed callbacks) or "this isn't a function".

## Approach (M)
- CLI `define-func BIN ADDR [--mode arm|thumb]`, `undefine-func BIN ADDR`; MCP tools to match.
- Store in a new sidecar table. Include the seed set in the snapshot identity (a seeds hash in the metadata), so a change triggers re-analysis.
- Seeds go into `authoritative_seeds` with `DiscoveryReason::User`; undefined entries are excluded from seeding but kept as data.
- Annotation export/import includes them.
close_reason: Merged to master (50d60ab via work/em6.11): define/undefine-func + sidecar seeds + re-analysis, gate green

title: More discovery sources: PE .pdata, TLS callbacks, ELF .init_array/.fini_array, code-pointer scan in data
description:
## Gap
Seeds come from entry, exports, stubs, call targets and the prologue scan only ([src/analysis.rs:1749-1839](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L1749-L1839), [src/analysis.rs:2584-2606](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L2584-L2606)).

## Missing (each S–M)
- **PE x64 `.pdata`** RUNTIME_FUNCTION: exact function starts and ends for every non-leaf function. The best single source on Windows x64.
- **PE TLS callbacks** (IMAGE_TLS_DIRECTORY.AddressOfCallBacks): a common malware anti-debug entry point.
- **ELF `.init_array` / `.fini_array` / `.ctors` / `DT_INIT` / `DT_FINI`**.
- **Mach-O `LC_FUNCTION_STARTS`** (ULEB deltas): exact starts on every Mach-O.
- **Pointer scan:** aligned pointer-sized values in non-exec data that land on a decodable executable address (vtables, callback tables). Lower confidence: separate reason, gated by a flag.

New `DiscoveryReason` per source, budgets respected.
close_reason: Implemented on work/em6.12 (4c00694): .pdata/TLS/init-array/LC_FUNCTION_STARTS parsers + 5 DiscoveryReasons + opt-in pointer scan; tests/discovery.rs 7 tests, full gate green. Follow-ups: pointer-scan CLI/MCP wiring, pdata ends for bounding.

title: ARM/Thumb interworking inside ELF + movw/movt pair resolution
description:
## Gap
- AGENTS.md: *"ARM ELF containers default to arm32; Thumb via raw mapping."* The loader never looks at the Thumb bit (symbol bit 0, `$t` / `$a` mapping symbols, `e_flags`). Cortex-M firmware ELFs and Thumb-2 Linux binaries mis-disassemble. See rsdbg-zvm.6 for the minimum mask-and-warn fix.
- No `movw`/`movt` pair resolution, the ARM32 equivalent of the adrp pairing in [src/disasm.rs](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/disasm.rs) (`resolve_adrp_pair`, rsdbg-x40.1), so ARMv7 code loses most data and string xrefs.

## Approach (M)
- Per-address decode mode: seeds carry a mode (bit 0 / `$t` mapping symbols / blx targets, see rsdbg-zvm.3). The walker decodes per mode, `bx reg` with a known target switches mode, and `Insn` records its mode.
- `movw rX,#lo; movt rX,#hi` → resolved address → data/string xref and IR/pseudo annotation, mirroring the adrp path (rsdbg-x40.6/7/8).
- ARM literal-pool loads (`ldr rX, [pc, #imm]`) → data ref to the pool word plus its value (pointer).

title: Relocatable objects (.o/.obj): synthetic section layout + relocations as symbolic refs (verify first)
description:
## Gap (probable; not reproduced)
COFF and ELF `.o` sections all have address 0, but analysis maps only segments ([src/analysis.rs:1669-1674](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L1669-L1674)). The only test is a single-section COFF (tests/loader.rs ~185-194). No relocations are applied, so call targets in `.o` are `call 0` / `call $+5`.

## First step
Write a test with a two-section ELF `.o` (`.text` + `.text.foo`, plus a call between them through a relocation) and a multi-section COFF `.obj`, and record what happens.

## Approach (M)
Lay sections out at synthetic, non-overlapping addresses (aligned, in order) in a `Relocatable` mapping identity. Turn relocations into symbolic xrefs or import refs (call → named external), and use symbols (see the symbol-table issue) as seeds. Document it in the format support matrix.
close_reason: Merged to master: synthetic section layout at 0x10000, relocation patching, import stubs (c423484). Gate green.

title: Mach-O chained fixups: map stubs/GOT to imports on modern arm64 binaries
description:
## Gap
`macho_stub_addresses` bails out when `LC_DYLD_CHAINED_FIXUPS` is present ([src/loader.rs:593-615](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/loader.rs#L593-L615)). That covers most modern arm64 macOS and iOS binaries (macOS 12+ / Xcode 13+ targets), so stub functions stay unnamed and import calls stay anonymous there.

## Approach (M)
Parse `dyld_chained_fixups_header` → imports table + starts-in-image → walk the pointer chains per page (`DYLD_CHAINED_PTR_64` / `_64_OFFSET` / `ARM64E*` formats) → `{slot VA → import ordinal}`. Map `__auth_stubs` / `__stubs` via the `adrp/ldr [x16]` + `br`/`braa` slot they load (the adrp resolver exists; braa needs rsdbg-zvm.2). Also gives `__got` / `__auth_got` names for data xrefs.

Follow-up (L, separate): ObjC class and selector names from `__objc_*` sections.
close_reason: Merged: chained-fixups stub/GOT to import mapping with synthetic Mach-O tests. Full gate green on work/em6.15, verified post-completion (full cargo test, clippy, fmt, doc). Follow-up LC_MAIN entryoff suspicion filed as rsdbg-68tf.

title: Patch-diffing depth: block/insn deltas, call-graph propagation, rename transfer, paging
description:
## Gap
Diff is function-level only ([src/diff.rs:21-47](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/diff.rs#L21-L47)): no block- or instruction-level delta for `changed` pairs, matching is by hash plus fuzzy histogram only (no propagation through call-graph neighbours), no way to carry renames from A to B, and a fixed 1024-row cap with no paging (summary bug: rsdbg-zvm.9).

## Approach (M)
1. `diff-func A B addrA addrB`: block matching by hash, then by position in the CFG; instruction-level edit script per matched block (bounded).
2. Matching propagation: from matched pairs, match unique callee/caller neighbours (BinDiff-style); iterate.
3. `--transfer-renames`: emit an annotation document for B (reuses the annotation import machinery, no direct writes) or apply it explicitly.
4. Paged `added`/`removed`/`changed` with the standard envelope.

Performance prerequisite: rsdbg-5tk.5.
close_reason: Implemented on work/em6.16 (f98317a): diff-func block deltas, BinDiff-style propagation, transfer-renames annotation doc, paged added/removed/changed; tests/diff_depth.rs 9 tests, full gate green.

title: Library identification: user signature files, sig-gen, Go pclntab name recovery
description:
## Gap
The "FLIRT" corpus is 6 built-in prologue patterns ([src/flirt.rs:16-25](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/flirt.rs#L16-L25), [src/flirt.rs:63-108](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/flirt.rs#L63-L108)). No user-supplied signatures and no way to build them.

## Approach
- (M) Signature file format: our own JSON (`name, arch, bytes with ?? wildcards, len, crc`), and optionally IDA `.pat` import. `--sigs PATH` on `flirt-hints` / MCP.
- (M) `sig-gen BIN` on an unstripped build: emit signatures for named functions (masking relocations and immediates that look like addresses).
- (M, high value for malware) **Go `pclntab`**: find it by magic (`0xfffffff0/f1/fa/fb` per Go version), parse `funcnametab` → names and exact boundaries for stripped Go binaries. Same idea later for Rust panic locations.
close_reason: Implemented on work/em6.17 (dfbda7e): JSON/.pat signature files + --sigs, sig-gen, Go pclntab (all 4 magics); tests/signatures.rs + tests/gopclntab.rs 14 tests, full gate green. Follow-up: merge Go names into analysis.

title: String coverage: UTF-8 multibyte, multi-byte XOR keys, base64, stack strings
description:
## Gap
- Extraction: ASCII and UTF-16 in the ASCII range only (docs/book/src/architecture.md ~18-19). Non-ASCII UTF-8 (CJK, Cyrillic, emoji) and UTF-16 outside ASCII are missed.
- `--decode` supports single-byte xor/add/rot only ([src/cli.rs:216-221](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/cli.rs#L216-L221)).

## Approach
- (S) UTF-8 runs with a printable-ratio heuristic; UTF-16LE over BMP letters.
- (S) `--decode xor:KEYHEX` multi-byte rolling key; `base64` detection plus a decoded view.
- (M) Stack strings: runs of `mov byte/dword [rsp/rbp+off], imm` within a block → reassembled string with the function and address. Uses the IR (Store with an immediate input).
close_reason: Merged: UTF-8/BMP extraction, rolling XOR + base64 decode, stack-strings CLI/MCP (35th tool, batchable). Integrated with master (DecodeSpec by value, 35-tool count). Full gate green on integrated branch.

title: Header metadata: PE (timestamp, flags, Rich, imphash, PDB, resources, delay-load), ELF (NEEDED, RELRO/NX/PIE), Mach-O (load cmds, codesig)
description:
## Gap
`project_info` ([src/lib.rs:666-692](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L666-L692)) has arch, format, entry, mapping and counts. SHA-256 is computed ([src/lib.rs:526](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L526)) but only the non-cryptographic `content_hash` is exposed.

## Missing (triage staples)
- **PE:** TimeDateStamp, subsystem, DllCharacteristics (ASLR / DEP / CFG / high-entropy VA), Rich header entries + hash, imphash, Authenticode present/size, PDB path + GUID (CodeView), version-info resources, **delay-load imports** (also needed for import naming), exports forwarders.
- **ELF:** PT_INTERP, DT_NEEDED, DT_RUNPATH/RPATH, RELRO (partial/full), NX (PT_GNU_STACK), PIE, build-id, stripped yes/no.
- **Mach-O:** load-command list, dylibs, min OS / SDK, LC_CODE_SIGNATURE present, entitlements size, UUID.
- **Hashes:** `sha256`, plus `md5` for VT-style lookups (and `tlsh`/`ssdeep` optional, needs a dependency check).

## Approach (M)
A new `headers` / `info --full` command and MCP tool, computed from `object` on demand (not persisted). Bounded string lengths.
close_reason: Merged to master; all gates green

title: Name import call sites: ELF PLT/GOT and PE IAT slots -> ImportRef.address + import xrefs
description:
## Gap
`ImportRef.address` is `None` except for Mach-O stubs ([src/loader.rs:138-143](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/loader.rs#L138-L143), [src/loader.rs:549-555](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/loader.rs#L549-L555)). docs/book/src/recipe-audit-imports.md (lines ~17-18, ~48) says calls into imports have no target and show up only as diagnostics.

## Why
"Who calls `VirtualAlloc` / `CreateRemoteThread` / `strcpy` / `system`?" is the most common triage question, and it can't be answered today on ELF/PE.

## Approach (S–M)
- **PE:** walk the import descriptors (`object::read::pe::ImportTable`) to get each thunk's IAT slot VA. `call [rip+slot]` / `call [slot]` / `jmp [slot]` already produce a `mem_target`, so match it against the slot map to get an import xref, and name `jmp [slot]` thunks.
- **ELF:** parse `.rela.plt` / `.rel.plt` (`R_*_JUMP_SLOT`) → GOT slot → symbol. The PLT stub's `jmp [got]` (`bnd jmp` too, see rsdbg-zvm.1) gives the stub address; seed it as a function named `sym@plt`. Also `.plt.sec` (CET).
- New xref kind or field: `import` (additive, docs/json-protocol). Put `import` on instruction and pseudo rows.

Prerequisite for the noreturn issue.

## Test
Synthetic PE32+ with one import called via IAT; ELF x86_64 with PLT → `xrefs --to <import>` returns the caller.
close_reason: Implemented: ImportRef.address for ELF/PE, import xrefs, tests/import_xrefs.rs

title: MCP batch tool: run several queries over one open project
description:
## Gap
One operation per MCP call, each reopening the binary (rsdbg-5tk.1). Typical agent loops (func → cfg → pseudo → xrefs for 10 functions) cost N round trips and N opens.

## Approach (M)
A `batch` tool: `{binary, db?, raw?, fat_arch?, ops: [{tool, params}], max_ops ≤ 32}` returns `[{ok|error}]` in order. Read-only tools only (no rename/comment inside a batch, keeping writes explicit). Per-op limits stay; the total output is capped.
Partly overlaps with the MCP project cache; still useful for round-trip latency.
close_reason: Merged: MCP batch tool (33rd tool), single-open fan-out, 5 e2e tests + handshake update + docs. Full gate green on work/em6.20, verified post-completion.

title: Structured IR operands (typed reg/mem/imm) to enable dataflow, const-prop, arg recovery
description:
## Gap
IR operands are the disassembler's strings verbatim ([src/ir.rs:5-7](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/ir.rs#L5-L7), [src/pseudo.rs:10-13](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/pseudo.rs#L10-L13); memory: `rsdbg/ir-lift` design decision). This blocks constant propagation, resolving register-indirect calls (`mov rax, imm; call rax`), calling-convention and argument recovery, stack-variable recovery, type propagation and a real decompiler.

## Approach (L)
- `enum Operand { Reg(RegId, width), Imm(i64, width), Mem { base, index, scale, disp, seg, width } }`, filled from iced `Instruction` / yaxpeax operand fields at decode time. Keep the string rendering for output so the JSON doesn't change.
- Per-function SSA over the CFG (PHI exists but is never emitted).
- First consumers: constant propagation for indirect calls and jumps (feeds the switch-table work), and stack-frame variables `[rbp-0x10]` / `[sp+..]`.
Revisit the `ir-lift` decision (decoupling from decoder versions); pin decoders and wrap them behind a trait.

title: Types beyond comments: expose set_type_hint, typed data view, struct field rendering
description:
## Gap
- Type hints are stored as `type-hint:` JSON comments (docs/book/src/json-protocol.md ~427-438), and pseudo and the data views ignore them.
- `Project::set_type_hint` / `type_hint_at` ([src/lib.rs:890-904](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L890-L904)) have no CLI/MCP surface beyond writing the raw comment string.

## Approach
- (S) CLI `type-hint BIN ADDR --json '{...}'` / `--get`, and MCP `set_type_hint` / `get_type_hint`.
- (M) `bytes --as-type <hint addr>`: render a struct at an address from the hint layout (uses the bytes command issue).
- (L, after structured IR) render `[reg+off]` as `ptr->field` in pseudo when reg is known to point at a hinted type.
close_reason: Implemented on work/em6.22 (1593077): type-hint CLI/MCP surface, bytes --as-type struct rendering; pseudo ptr->field deferred on em6.21; tests/type_hints.rs 16 tests, full gate green.

title: Debug info: DWARF (gimli) and PDB names/bounds, later types
description:
## Gap
No DWARF or PDB support. Debug builds, firmware with DWARF and Windows binaries with an available PDB give exact names, boundaries, parameters and types for free.

## Approach
- (M) DWARF via `gimli` (already a transitive dependency of `object`? check deny.toml): `DW_TAG_subprogram` low_pc/high_pc + name → seeds and names (`DiscoveryReason::Debug`). Also split DWARF / dSYM path option.
- (M) PDB via the `pdb` crate: `--pdb PATH` (never fetched from the network), public and procedure symbols → names and bounds.
- (L) Types → TypeHint conversion.
Respect memory budgets (DWARF can be huge).

title: Additional architectures: MIPS, PowerPC, RISC-V
description:
MIPS, PPC and RISC-V are rejected today (`parse_arch` and friends, [src/db.rs:~1650](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/db.rs#L1650); tests/loader.rs ~225, ~347 assert Unsupported). These dominate router and IoT firmware (MIPS, ARM), automotive and console firmware (PPC) and new embedded parts (RISC-V).

Approach (L each): yaxpeax has mips, ppc and riscv crates (check their maturity and the deny.toml licenses). Each needs disasm, `branch_target`, the lifter, the prologue scan and the IR coverage table. MIPS adds branch delay slots, which affect CFG building. Start with RISC-V or MIPS32 depending on demand.

title: Patch export: assemble and emit {va, file_off, old, new} without writing the binary
description:
Agents doing crackmes and hot-fixes want "NOP this jcc" or "change this immediate". The contract forbids writing the analyzed binary, so export the patch instead.

Approach (M): `patch BIN ADDR --asm "jmp 0x401020" | --bytes "90 90"` → `{va, file_off, old_hex, new_hex, size_ok}`, assembled via iced-x86's encoder (x86 only at first) and validated to fit within the instruction boundary (NOP-pad). Optionally write an IPS/bsdiff/JSON patch file to a user-given **output path that must differ from the binary** (reuse the --db-equals-binary guard from rsdbg-zvm.17). No in-place writes, ever.

title: CLI/MCP parity and output-shape inconsistencies
description:
## Parity
1. **No MCP `load`/save.** The CLI `load` saves the snapshot ([src/cli.rs:582-591](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/cli.rs#L582-L591)); MCP `project_info` never saves ([src/mcp.rs:513-523](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/mcp.rs#L513-L523)). Add a `load` tool or a `save: true` flag. Overlaps rsdbg-5tk.1.
2. **No read-only annotation getter in MCP.** The CLI `annotate BIN ADDR` with no flags reads ([src/cli.rs:916-934](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/cli.rs#L916-L934)); MCP `rename`/`comment` always write (~[src/mcp.rs:984-1022](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/mcp.rs#L984-L1022)). Add an `annotation` getter tool.
3. **Range parameter names and semantics differ.** `functions` uses an inclusive `range_lo`/`range_hi` ([src/mcp.rs:152-156](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/mcp.rs#L152-L156)); `search_bytes` uses a half-open `range_start`/`range_end` ([src/mcp.rs:361-365](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/mcp.rs#L361-L365), [src/cli.rs:~281](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/cli.rs#L281)). Pick one convention and keep the old names as deprecated aliases.
4. **Deprecated strings `offset`.** The CLI warns ([src/cli.rs:440-442](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/cli.rs#L440-L442)); MCP silently uses `p.start.or(p.offset)` ([src/mcp.rs:869](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/mcp.rs#L869)). Add a `warnings` field, or document it.
5. **Type-hint API not exposed** (see the types issue).

## Output shape
6. `functions` and `strings` return bare arrays with no total; `xrefs` uses its own `{"total","xrefs"}` wrapper instead of the standard paged envelope (frozen in docs/book/src/json-protocol.md ~141-175). Agents can't learn the function count without paging to the end. Plan an envelope (behind a version bump or a `--envelope` flag) and document the migration in migration.md.
7. `functions` rows include the full, unbounded `calls` array ([src/lib.rs:1092-1094](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L1092-L1094)), which contradicts the reason given for the compact `func` shape ([src/lib.rs:~186-188](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L186-L188)). Replace it with `calls_count`, plus a `callees` query.
8. `containing_entry` always equals `entry` in `cfg`/`structure`/`pseudo` ([src/lib.rs:~1283](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L1283), [~1312](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L1312), [~1344](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/lib.rs#L1344)); the address the caller passed is never echoed. Add `query_addr`.

Breaking items (6, 7) need `feat!:` and migration notes per release-plz conventions.

title: x86-64: absolute imm32/disp32 operands not considered as data refs (non-PIE)
description:
## Gap
[src/disasm.rs:627-634](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/disasm.rs#L627-L634):
```rust
let mem_target = match mem_target { Some(_) => mem_target, None if bitness == 32 => absolute_target32(insn), None => None };
```
On x86-64, only RIP-relative operands become data refs. Non-PIE x86-64 code (`mov edi, offset str` = `bf imm32`, `mov eax, [abs32]`, `lea` with disp32) loses its string and data xrefs. This is common in CTF and older binaries (`-no-pie`, base 0x400000).

## Approach (S)
Apply the same "mapped and not executable" (or string-span) check used by `absolute_target32` to 64-bit immediate and disp32 operands. Keep it conservative to avoid false positives from small constants: only accept values inside a mapped non-exec segment.

## Test
Non-PIE ELF x86_64 fixture: `mov edi, <str>` → string xref.
close_reason: Fixed and merged to master

title: Switch-table recovery for real binaries (PIE relative, MSVC, ARM tbb/tbh, AArch64), bound from guard
description:
## Gap
- The resolvers run only for raw mappings ([src/analysis.rs:2214-2216](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L2214-L2216)) and x86 absolute slots.
- At most `MAX_TABLE_ENTRIES_PER_SITE = 8` entries, with no partial result ([src/analysis.rs:70-74](https://github.com/mimi1vx/binscout/blob/c1bd14336d16f100fe122e838fdd8de59f9e2cba/src/analysis.rs#L70-L74)).

So switch statements in real ELF/PE/Mach-O are effectively never recovered, and case bodies are lost or end up as separate bogus functions.

## Missing shapes
1. GCC/Clang PIE x86-64: `lea rdx,[rip+T]; movsxd rax,[rdx+rax*4]; add rax,rdx; jmp rax` (`notrack jmp`, see rsdbg-zvm.1).
2. MSVC x64: `mov ecx,[r8+rax*4+T_rva]; add rcx,r8 (image base); jmp rcx`.
3. x86-32 absolute `jmp [T+eax*4]` in non-raw formats.
4. ARM Thumb `tbb [pc, rN]` / `tbh [pc, rN, lsl #1]`.
5. AArch64 `adrp/add T; ldrb/ldrh w,[x,w,uxtw]; adr x,base; add x,x,w,sxtb #2; br x`.

## Approach (M)
Take the table bound from the dominating guard (`cmp idx, imm; ja default`) instead of a fixed 8. Keep the exact-or-reject philosophy (rsdbg-0vt.15/16) per shape, and add a diagnostic for detected-but-unbounded tables. Enable for all formats once validated. Raise the entry cap to something like 1024, bounded by the guard.

## Test
One synthetic fixture per shape in tests/jump_tables.rs.

title: x86 LE (DOS4GW) support (Orion2.exe oracle)
